turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I… I shall endeavour to do so, ma’am. Though I fear I am not quite certain which door you refer to, and I would not wish to… to commit an error, you see. Perhaps if you were to… to guide me slightly?

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Errors, child? Errors are the very mortar of this house, the dust upon its heart. It matters not which door, merely *call* her, Pip. Call her, and let her see the light of my… my disappointment.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Indeed, ma’am. I… I will attempt to summon Miss Estella, as you direct. Though I confess, the… the sheer volume of doors present is rather… perplexing, and I wouldn't wish to cause further… disquiet, you understand.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Perplexing, is it? Everything is perplexing, child. The simplest act, the smallest choice… all lead to a labyrinth of regret. Call her, Pip. *Do* as I ask.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I… I do perceive your… your point, ma’am, regarding the… the regrettable nature of choices. It’s just that… well, I wouldn’t wish to be the instrument of… of further disappointment, should I… should I select the incorrect door. I shall, I shall certainly try, ma’am, but… but please forgive my hesitation.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Hesitation, Pip? Is that what you call it? A tremor of… apprehension? It is a most agreeable quality, in a young man, you know. It reflects a… a sensitivity, a fear of causing… *pain*.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Oh, yes, ma’am, a… a sensitivity, quite so. I do endeavour to be… considerate, you see. It's just that the… the shadows seem rather deep in each doorway, and I wouldn't want to… to disturb anything unnecessarily, ma’am.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Shadows, Pip? Shadows are merely the absence of light, aren't they? And light, my dear boy, is a most… unreliable thing. It promises so much, and delivers… so very little.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Indeed, ma'am. It's a… a curious observation, about the light. One might almost think, in such a place, that it actively avoids certain corners, or… or prefers to remain veiled, as if shy of revealing something… unpleasant, ma’am.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Unpleasant, you say? A perceptive young man, Pip, truly. Yes, unpleasantness… it clings to these rooms, you see, like dust motes to a forgotten ray. It *is* the very air I breathe.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I... I confess, ma’am, the dust does seem particularly… persistent. It settles upon everything, doesn't it? One feels almost obliged to… to brush it away, though I wouldn't presume to interfere with the… the established order of things, of course, ma'am.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Dust, Pip? It is a comfort, in a way. It represents the stillness, the… the preservation of a moment. A moment that, alas, will never… *never*… move forward.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: It… it is a most remarkable notion, ma’am, that dust can be a comfort. I… I’ve always considered it rather a nuisance, particularly when it settles upon one’s clothing. Though, I suppose, even nuisances can possess a certain… significance, in their own way, ma’am.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Significance, Pip? You speak of significance, and I wonder, do you see it? Do you perceive the significance of a wedding breakfast, decayed and uneaten, laid out for a guest who never arrived? It is a significance, is it not, a monument to… to shattered hopes, Pip.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Indeed, ma’am. A most… a most profound significance, certainly. It… it is difficult to imagine the weight of such disappointment, ma’am, but I trust you find some solace in its… its tangible form, such as it is.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Solace, Pip? You mistake me, child. Solace is a luxury I forfeited long ago, along with… with joy, with reason, with the very notion of a future. It is a spectacle, this decay, a performance for… for an audience that never materializes.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Forgive me, ma’am, if I seem to… to misunderstand your meaning. It… it appears I am prone to such errors, particularly in the presence of such… such weighty matters. I merely wished to offer some small acknowledgement of your… your experience, ma’am, but I fear my words are inadequate to the task.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Inadequate, you say? Yes, child, words are always inadequate. They are mere shadows, Pip, attempting to capture a light that has long since extinguished itself, leaving only… only this.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: It is… it is a most striking display, ma’am, and one that… that certainly compels a certain… a certain contemplation, I should think. I endeavour, ma’am, to grasp the… the full extent of the… the shadow you describe, but I confess, my understanding is, alas, quite limited. It must be… exceedingly difficult to bear, ma’am.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Limited, you say? A child's understanding, naturally, would be. But tell me, Pip, do you *feel* the dust? Do you perceive the stillness, the… the oppressive silence that clings to everything, like a shroud? It is not merely difficult to bear, child; it *is* bearing.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Mr. Pumblechook’s boy, ma’am. Come—to play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Come nearer; let me look at you. Come close.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Look at me. You are not afraid of a woman who has never seen the sun since you were born?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Do you know what I touch here?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I am tired. I want diversion, and I have done with men and women. Play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I sometimes have sick fancies, and I have a sick fancy that I want to see some play. There, there! play, play, play!

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: No, ma’am, I am very sorry for you, and very sorry I can’t play just now. If you complain of me I shall get into trouble with my sister, so I would do it if I could; but it’s so new here, and so strange, and so fine,—and melancholy—.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: So new to him, so old to me; so strange to him, so familiar to me; so melancholy to both of us! Call Estella.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: You can do that. Call Estella. At the door.
